findings.evidence: Proof body lines 231-236 uses `hS` only inside `hord : T.OrdConnected`. `StarConvex.add_smul_mem` at upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Star.lean:313; `Convex.starConvex` at upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Basic.lean:58.
findings.fix: State `theorem geometricPathLength_eq_sSup (hS : StarConvex ℝ x S) (hx : x ∈ S) : geometricPathLength S x v = sSup {s | 0 ≤ s ∧ x + s • v ∈ S}`, proving `hord` from `StarConvex.add_smul_mem` (for `0 ≤ u ≤ t` with `x + t • v ∈ S`, apply it with `y := t • v` and coefficient `u / t`); the convex case is then `hS.starConvex hx`.
findings.issue: `geometricPathLength_eq_sSup (hS : Convex ℝ S) (hx : x ∈ S)` is stronger than the proof needs: the only use of `hS` is to make `T = {s | 0 ≤ s ∧ x + s • v ∈ S}` `OrdConnected`, which follows from star-convexity about `x` alone. Supports of interest here (deformed/two-centre profiles, level sets of a non-convex density) are star-shaped without being convex.

findings.evidence: Lines 191-195: the only occurrences of `hSb` and `hv` are `ne_top_of_le_ne_top hSb.ediam_ne_top (… volume_setOf_le_ediam (x := x) hv)`. Roadmap NuclearMedium/README.md:393 lists "A uniform slab of thickness `L` with normal incidence" as a Layer 0 example.
findings.fix: Replace `hSb` and `hv` by `hfin : volume {s : ℝ | 0 ≤ s ∧ x + s • v ∈ S} ≠ ⊤`; keep the bounded/unit-direction case as a one-line corollary obtained from `volume_setOf_le_ediam hv` and `hSb.ediam_ne_top`.
findings.issue: `densityWeightedPathLength_le` carries `hSb : Bornology.IsBounded S` and `hv : ‖v‖ = 1`, both used only at lines 193-195 to show the ray-set has finite volume (via `volume_setOf_le_ediam`). The real hypothesis is finiteness of that measure, and the bounded-support form excludes the roadmap's uniform-slab example, whose support is unbounded while every ray-set still has finite measure.

summary: Two hypotheses are stronger than the proofs need: `geometricPathLength_eq_sSup` assumes full convexity where star-convexity about the production point is what the argument uses, and `densityWeightedPathLength_le` assumes a bounded support plus a unit direction only as a proxy for finiteness of the ray-set measure, which excludes the roadmap's slab example.
